newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-GIL THREATENS TO WITHDRAW ATLETICO FROM CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GIL THREATENS TO WITHDRAW ATLETICO FROM CUP.

text.p: Atletico Madrid owner Jesus Gil has suspended his team's trip to Barcelona for Wednesday's Spanish Cup quarter-final in a row over player bans.

Gil is to decide in the hours before the game whether to withdraw the club from the competition in protest at the suspension of three key players for incidents in Sunday's 3-2 league defeat at Real Betis.
"They want to humiliate Atletico. I am prepared to suffer the punishment," said Gil, whose team could be banned from next year's competition and face a heavy fine.
Atletico are appealing gainst the bans imposed by the Spanish Football Federation's disciplinary committee on Tuesday.
The appeal, to be heard on Wednesday morning, will determine whether or not Juan Eduardo Esnaider, Diego Simeone and Delfi Geli will be able to play in the Cup clash.
The outspoken Atletico supremo had already threatened to create problems if the decisions went against his club, and his move is being interpreted as a way of pressurising the appeal committee.
Argentine internationals Esnaider and Simeone each face two-match bans, while defender Geli will miss one game.
Esnaider's punishment came for trying to head-butt an opponent, while Simeone and Geli were suspended for insulting the referee after the final whistle.
But coach Radomir Antic, who was also accused of insulting match officials, escaped without punishment.
